senses.sense_definition: An elastic, insoluble protein that forms a fibrous network during blood coagulation.

examples.text: The <w>fibrin</w> network acts as a scaffold to stabilize the blood clot.
During injury, thrombin converts fibrinogen into <w>fibrin</w> to stop the bleeding.

senses.sense_definition: A white, fibrous substance produced when blood coagulates.

examples.text: The wound was covered by a layer of <w>fibrin</w> to prevent further blood loss.
Laboratory tests showed high levels of <w>fibrin</w> in the patient's blood sample.

senses.sense_definition: A protein found in cereal grains that is similar in composition to animal fibrin.

examples.text: Researchers identified a substance in the seeds that functions like <w>fibrin</w>.
This vegetable <w>fibrin</w> is essential for the structural integrity of the grain.

senses.sense_definition: To apply a sealant made of fibrin to a surgical site to stop bleeding or close a flap.

examples.text: The surgeon decided to <w>fibrin</w> the area to ensure the wound healed properly.
They will <w>fibrin</w> the surgical site to minimize post-operative bleeding.
